research_rationale:
EO 11813 (Oct. 7, 1974; 39 FR 36317) directed that a cooperative education student under a Schedule B appointment may be converted noncompetitively to a career or career-conditional appointment if four conditions in Section 2 items (1)-(4) are met, defined cooperative education (Sec. 1), directed the Civil Service Commission to issue regulations (Sec. 3), revoked EO 11202 (Sec. 4) and took effect immediately (Sec. 5). Section 4 of EO 12015 (signed Oct. 26, 1977; 42 FR 56947) states, in the Federal Register OCR text, "Executive Order No. 11813 of October 7, 1974-, is hereby revoked." The American Presidency Project page for EO 12015 gives the same sentence cleanly: "Executive Order No. 11813 of October 7, 1974, is hereby revoked." EO 12015 contains no effective-date clause, so the revocation operates from its signing date. The cross-check is the held 5 U.S.C. 3301 note in jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt, which states that Executive Order No. 11813 "was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12015, Oct. 26, 1977, 42 F.R. 56947". The order has no own-terms end, so the express revocation is its first end and all four dossier clauses end together on 1977-10-26.

savings.reason: Conversions completed under Section 2 before Oct. 26, 1977 were executed acts and EO 12015 Section 4 does not undo them. EO 12015 sets a similar conversion rule for career-related work-study programs, but that is a new command in a new order, not a continuation of EO 11813. No held source shows an independent command that still depends on EO 11813.
